text:
Water-side fluid volume of the serpentine cold plate, meshed.

**Geometry (from the request):** plate envelope 60 × 40 × 8 mm; channel 4 mm wide, 5 mm deep, milled from the top face (so fluid spans z = 3…8 mm); three passes along the 60 mm length with 3 mm of metal between them (pass centrelines y = 13, 20, 27 mm). Inlet is the open end at x = 0 on pass 1, outlet the open end at x = 60 mm on pass 3; the two U-bends are internal. Only the water volume is meshed — no solid region.

**Measured on the built geometry / mesh:** bounding box 0…60 × 11…29 × 3…8 mm → channel width 4.0 mm, rib gaps 3.0 mm, depth 5.0 mm, three passes centred across the 40 mm width; inlet and outlet face areas 20.0 mm² each (4 × 5); fluid volume 3.560e-6 m³ = centreline length 178 mm × 20 mm² exactly. Built in mm, scaled once by 0.001 to metres before export — mesh bbox is 0.06 m long.

**Mesh:** blockMesh background + snappyHexMesh (feature snap, no layers), 0.5 mm base cells → 28 480 cells, all hexahedra (8 across the width, 10 through the depth). checkMesh: Mesh OK, max non-orthogonality 15.8, max skewness 0.156, max aspect 1.38, total volume matches CAD to 1e-7 relative. Patches `inlet` (patch), `outlet` (patch), `walls` (wall) named on the faces as constructed, not by bounding-box position.

**Assumptions I made (not given):** pass direction along the 60 mm length and the 18 mm pass band centred across the 40 mm width; U-bend corners left square rather than filleted to a 2 mm cutter radius; bend end-walls set 2 mm in from the x = 0 / x = 60 faces so the turns stay inside the plate; mesh resolution 0.5 mm and no boundary layers.

**Not checked:** nothing was verified about the aluminium solid (it was not meshed), and no y⁺-driven layer sizing was attempted since no flow rate was given.
